brief: McElligott (Nomura, via The Market Ear) argues an energy shock is spreading into broader macro. China has stopped releasing reserves to cushion the shock and is instead rebuilding inventories and lifting offers, pushing Shanghai crude well above Brent; a broadening shortage of crude, refining capacity, diesel and VLCCs is turning this into an inflation and rates problem, not just an oil story. Oil volatility is spilling into bonds: MOVE has caught a bid and separated from VIX, and demand for upside rate protection (payer skew, vol of vol) is nearing multi-year highs. The stated risk sequence is conditional and not yet realized: another leg higher in energy would ignite rates volatility, negative convexity from dealer swaption/VIX-option hedging would amplify the move, and broader asset beta would finally break, with a renewed yen rally adding a second carry-unwind channel. Currently equities treat it as noise and sit near highs; the tail risk is building but has not yet broken markets. Preferred hedges named: dollar, energy equities, commodity carry, rates trend, long volatility; weakening: bonds, equities, gold, credit, crypto.
